To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we introduce a new dataset and a novel setting for few-shot learning that mimics real-world scenarios; (2) we show that the proposed online few-shot setting is challenging, and current few-shot models are not able to perform well in this setting; (3) we propose a novel model, called Contextualized Few-Shot Learning (CFS), that is able to perform online few-shot classification; and (4) we show that our model achieves state-of-the-art results

(1) online contextualized few-shot is a promising new paradigm that is more representative of the real world than standard few-shot learning, (2) our proposed dataset is the first of its kind, (3) we show that the context in our dataset is indeed useful, and (4) we demonstrate that a few-shot learning algorithm that is trained in this setting outperforms standard few-shot learning algorithms on our proposed dataset and other standard benchmarks

1) the context in which an episode occurs has an impact on the performance of a few-shot learning algorithm; 2) the context of an episode can be inferred from the visual information available at the beginning of the episode; and 3) a model can be trained in this setting to infer the context and improve performance.
